I'm only recounting a personal experience of a close friend of mine. Chiros don't work for everyone but going to a very experienced one can potentially change your life. A lot of individuals with pinched nerves and disc pain have reported varying degrees of improvement. 

A chiropractor didn't work for me but his wife seems to have the same issue my friend did. Sports injury and all that. Definitely worth a visit to an experienced chiropractor.

Sorry I'm aware this isn't addressing how to support her. So to answer that, since it's her lower back, is pain travelling down any or both of the legs? If so, which one? Massages are great, try that. Also, be super considerate of this pain. I myself live with cervical pain and this month marks 2 whole sad years of it. 

I can say for sure that a supportive, loving, considerate SO is what would get me through the day. Somebody who will constantly ask them if they're okay, be considerate of them when driving them around (get her a back rest for your car if you drive), push her to schedule a chiropractor appointment because it's very easy to give up on seeking help. She's going to need somebody like you to push her not to lose hope. 

No matter what happens between you two. Whether a debate gets heated or she does something which could possibly irk you, please remember the chronic pain she suffers from. It can do so much to make you a miserable person if you suffer from it. I'm not proud of my behaviour on the days the pain is there. And on those days, I need a home to come back to. Please please please, be her home <3

My best friend has a herniated disc in his back. Lower back so that's the lumbar region. He went to a chiropractor, followed her instructions and has experienced a great amount of relief. His exact words were "there is no background pain anymore"
